candidate_structure.information_flow: The first call forms one self-contained executable closure and removes construction provenance from its handoff. The final call consumes that complete closure with public obligations but without anchor-policy visibility. A derivable contradiction with those obligations triggers revocation of predecessor semantic authority and obligation-grounded reconstitution within the same single lineage; the final call emits one policy.
candidate_structure.name: Contradiction-Triggered Semantic Revocation Relay
candidate_structure.organization: two-call sequential lineage with a provenance firewall and one defeasible semantic-authority edge

calls.objective: Form exactly one self-contained executable policy closure from the supplied evidence and public obligations, remove anchor-relative construction provenance from the handoff, and pass the complete executable artifact forward.

Compare represented predecessor commitments with explicit public obligations, retain closure authority absent a derivable incompatibility, or revoke that authority upon such evidence and reconstitute the single artifact under obligation authority, then emit one complete policy.

mode_certificate.champion_limitation: The champion cannot withdraw causal authority from an inherited closure whose represented semantics contradict an explicit public obligation.
mode_certificate.not_local_refinement: The mutation introduces defeasible causal inheritance and an evidence-triggered authority transition, a control capability absent from unconditional closure reconciliation and distinct from pre-construction frame changes.
mode_certificate.observable_effect: Upon qualifying contradiction evidence, the final policy is no longer constrained by the conflicting inherited commitment; otherwise the closure retains semantic authority.
mode_certificate.state_transition: The final call moves from closure-authoritative state to closure-revoked state and reconstitutes the single executable artifact under public-obligation authority before emission.
mode_certificate.trigger: A concrete incompatibility derivable between a represented semantic commitment in the predecessor closure and an explicit public obligation visible to the final call.

qualitative_hypothesis.causal_change: Make the predecessor-to-final authority edge defeasible: a public-obligation contradiction revokes inherited semantic authority and transfers control to obligation-grounded reconstitution.
qualitative_hypothesis.expected_effect: The lineage can escape a causally binding but contradicted closure while preserving a single complete executable lineage and one final policy.
qualitative_hypothesis.falsifier: all-valid matched majority and strict-median contract, with no score
qualitative_hypothesis.observed_bottleneck: The champion grants the inherited executable closure continuing semantic authority even when its represented commitments are incompatible with explicit public obligations.

structural_mutation.after: The final call treats closure authority as defeasible and revokes it only upon deriving a concrete incompatibility with an explicit public obligation, then reconstitutes the single policy artifact under obligation authority.
structural_mutation.before: The final call receives a provenance-blind executable closure whose current semantics remain the mandatory frame for reconciliation and emission.
structural_mutation.factor: public-obligation contradiction-triggered revocation of predecessor semantic authority
structural_mutation.why_structural: This changes the causal authority and state-transition semantics of the predecessor edge from unconditional inheritance to evidence-triggered revocation without adding a role, gate, reviewer, or parallel path.
